q: Can any CBAM verifier verify our plant, or does it need our sector?
title: CBAM verifier scopes: does yours fit?
short: It needs your sector. CBAM verifiers are accredited for numbered activity groups, such as I for cement or VIII for iron, steel and aluminium products. A verifier without the group covering your goods may not verify your plant, and other verifiers check this scope before relying on its report.
audience: Indian CBAM goods producers comparing verifier quotes

sections.h: The groups on a CBAM accreditation certificate
ul: I: calcined clay, cement clinker, cement, aluminous cement.
V: sintered ore, pig iron, DRI, crude steel.
VIII: iron or steel products, aluminium products.
L: carbon capture, use and storage. LI: electricity imported into the EU. LII: indirect emissions.

sections.h: Match your plant before you match the price
ul: Re-rolling mill making bars, coil or pipes from bought billets or slabs: VIII.
Sponge iron plant with an electric furnace and a rolling mill: V for the DRI and crude steel, VIII for the rolled products.
Aluminium smelter casting ingots: VII. Extruder making profiles from bought billet: VIII.
Cement or clinker plant: I, which always comes with LII, because indirect emissions count for cement.
Urea or NPK plant: IV with LII; an ammonia unit adds II.
Sinter plant: V with LII. Other iron, steel and aluminium goods do not count indirect emissions, so a plant needing only VI, VII or VIII does not need LII.

p: No verifier can be accredited for LII by itself. It comes only together with group I, II, III, IV or V, and a body granting those groups must check the verifier's competence on indirect emissions too. If your goods carry indirect emissions and you buy electricity under a power purchase agreement or over a direct line, ask whether the team has checked smart meter data, single line diagrams and PPAs before. If you use a power plant's verified emission factor instead of a default, that plant's verifier must have held the scope for its goods plus LII when it signed, and the report must cover the same year your goods were made.

sections.h: It also matters for your suppliers
p: When you use a supplier's verified figure for a precursor, your verifier checks that the supplier's verifier held a valid accreditation for that sector at the time. A Raipur sponge iron supplier verified by a firm accredited only for group VIII would not pass. Ask your precursor suppliers for their verifier's scope as well as the report.

ol: Which activity groups are on your CBAM certificate, and which national accreditation body issued it?
Will the accreditation still be valid when you issue our verification report?
Will the lead auditor speak English and will one auditor on the team speak our language? The Commission requires both.
